First question

What are they doing, how deep, and how close?

The activity, depth and distance to the asset decide whether a Network Access Permit and added controls are required.

Face-to-face site check

1

Confirm the work scope

Ask where they will excavate, bore or drill; the planned depth; equipment being used; and which SAPN asset is nearby.

2

See the current information

Confirm the work area matches their Before You Dig Australia enquiry. Plans alone do not prove the exact cable position.

3

Check whether a NAP is triggered

Use the depth-and-distance triggers below. If it is required, the contractor must hold it while working.

4

Check the permit is in effect

A prepared NAP is not enough. It must be authorised by an SAPN authorised switching officer before work starts.

5

Match the controls to the zone

Confirm the work method, certified locator, potholing, observer and any non-auto or de-energisation conditions required by the NAP.

6

Check completion

Ground and asset protection must be reinstated to the required specification. The NAP is returned after the work and reinstatement are complete.

NAP trigger check

A NAP is required when excavation is deeper than the stated depth and within the stated vicinity.

>0.3 mNear underground cables, as controlled by the voltage-specific zones.
>0.3 mWithin 3 m of a pole, light column, manhole, padmount transformer, cubicle, pit, pillar or switching cabinet.
>0.5 mWithin 10 m of an electricity or telecommunications tower.
>0.2 mWithin 2 m of a substation fence, wall or property boundary.
>0.3 mWithin the distance stated on attached infrastructure signage, including SWER transformer poles.

Stop and escalate

  • No required NAP, or the NAP has not been authorised.
  • The work area, method, depth or asset differs from the permit and BYDA information.
  • A required locator, pothole, observer, non-auto condition or isolation is missing.
  • An exclusion zone is breached or a cable or conduit is unexpectedly exposed.
  • The asset, footing, earth, conduit, cover or cable may have been disturbed or damaged.

Unplanned exclusion-zone breach: stop work and call Faults & Emergencies immediately on 13 13 66.

Hydro-vac still has the Section 9 nozzle-distance and pressure limits. “Permitted” never overrides the NAP or site-specific controls.

Hydro-vac limits
200 mmMinimum separation between nozzle tip and subsoil. Do not touch or insert the nozzle into the soil.
2000 psiMaximum working water pressure for general work (13,790 kPa).
1200 psiMaximum where critical cables are identified, including paper-lead and fibre-optic cables (8,274 kPa).
Foundations, earthing and consumer mains
  • Never cut, grind or disturb an infrastructure concrete footing.
  • A substation earth grid can extend beyond the fence. Excavation deeper than 200 mm within 2 m requires a Network Access Request.
  • Where SWER earthing signage is present, follow the stated distance. If signage or a distance is absent, contact the local Customer Solutions Manager.
  • Consumer-mains excavation at a pole, pit or pillar requires an approved connection, compliance with the Service & Installation Rules and Section 7.1, no other open excavation, a trench under 350 mm wide and under 600 mm deep, plus any site-specific requirements.
Exposed cables and reinstatement
  • Do not leave an exposed underground cable unsupervised.
  • An exposed cable may need to be de-energised or the affected HV asset placed non-auto; capture this in the NAP request. The exception noted is LV cable within conduit.
  • Restore backfill, coverboard and other protection to the original specification and return ground level to its previous level.
  • Return the NAP after work and TS085-compliant reinstatement are complete.

How to read this

Compare the reduction in take-home pay, tax saved and possible future balance—not just the amount contributed. The planner assumes the extra amount is salary-sacrificed and deducts 15% contributions tax.

Compare purchased leave

Each purchased week costs one week of the selected classification's base rate, spread evenly over 26 fortnightly pays.

The workdays setting only converts purchased weeks into extra days off. It does not change the salary calculation.

Assumptions

Purchased leave is treated as a pre-tax reduction equal to the selected weekly base rate multiplied by the weeks purchased. Employer super remains calculated on the full base-rate earnings. Overtime, allowances and the other settings currently entered in the pay calculator remain included.

Actual payroll treatment can depend on your employer's purchased-leave policy, including eligibility, accrual, cancellation and super treatment. Use this as an estimate and confirm the arrangement before applying.

Portable switching equipment

This is a training and quick-reference transcription of E2792–E2797. Confirm the current approved drawing, procedure, switching program and onsite risk assessment before work.

Resistor load box · E2792

Supply item 1008117 · for lightly loaded transformers rated up to 200 kVA where ferroresonance may occur during single-pole HV switching.

Use when

  • Single-pole switching on the HV side is necessary.
  • Switching 33 kV transformers.
  • Switching 11 kV or 7.6 kV transformers where ferroresonance is a perceived risk, including remote single-pole switching on more than 150 m of HV conductor or single-phase 11 kV UD transformers supplied by HV underground cable.
Service intervalReturn every 12 months
Maximum switching periodComplete within 30 minutes

Critical sequence

Neutral first on · last off

  • Maintain prescribed clearances and wear the specified linesperson, leather and cotton gloves for connections and disconnections.
  • Check lead continuity before use and again before storage.
  • Earth the box using the supplied earth cable.
  • Connect leads on the transformer side of LV fuses.
  • Keep clear of flammable material and support lead weight with the preformed grip on pole-mounted transformers.
  • Allow adequate cooling time after switching.

Source: E2792 sheets 1–2 · also refers to DSM-0437

11 kV & 33 kV liquid interrupters · E2794

Typical applications

  • De-energising transformers over 200 kVA on overhead systems.
  • Underground cables and ABC at overhead isolators.
  • Overhead lines within the applicable device capacity.
  • Changing open points between main feeders.

Pre-use checks

  • Liquid must be clear, clean and at or above the marked level. Return any cloudy, black or low-liquid unit.
  • Glass and outer surfaces clean and free from cracks; contact surfaces free from corrosion.
  • Operating/trip lever rotates freely.
  • Actuating spring has no wire-diameter-sized gap between turns.
Perchlorethylene and glass unit

Wear the required PPE, load only in open space, point the open end away from people and follow JSWP 134D. Liquid replacement must not be performed in the field.

Installation and operation

  • Apply jointing compound OC7968 to contact surfaces.
  • Install with the tripping-mechanism end upward and away from the operator, in the right-side contacts.
  • Use an approved operating stick and accessories; trip with firm, even pressure without striking or side-loading the lever.
  • Carry in the purpose-designed box, in the loaded mode, and store vertically.

Source: E2794 sheets 1–4 · capacities refer to E2806–E2808

Loadbuster interrupters · E2795
11 kV modelEB9700 · 25 kV nominal · 600 A
33 kV modelEB9701 · 34.5 kV nominal · 600 A
Open length0.65 m / 0.8 m
Weight3 kg

Do not exceed the tool’s maximum voltage or current rating. EB9701 is used for 11 kV, SWER 19 kV and 33 kV, but not orange substation-style SMD-1A or SMD-50 fuses.

Before operation

  • Check the tool is clean and undamaged.
  • Extend approximately 100 mm and release to check the internal spring returns correctly.
  • Read the operations counter and confirm the service card is current.

Operating sequence

  1. Orient the Loadbuster in front of the attachment hook, facing the operator.
  2. Attach the anchor to the far-side device attachment hook.
  3. Attach the pull-ring hook; confirm the latch prevents disengagement.
  4. Pull downward with a firm, steady motion to maximum extension.
  5. Remove the anchor first, then roll the tool off the fully opened pull ring.
  6. Release the resetting latch and close firmly until the orange band is no longer visible.
  7. Repeat the 100 mm spring-return check, read the counter and store in its case.
Routine serviceEvery 500 operations
Allowed overlapMaximum 50 operations
End of lifeDo not use after 5000 operations
High-load useMay require earlier servicing

Arc stranglers · E2796

Used in equipment including Mk 3 padmount transformers, Brown Boveri NAL switching cubicles and mobile transformer units. Operating limitations are in E3000.

Closing

  1. Pull the sleeve down to reset.
  2. Insert the blade into the bottom contacts horizontally with the shotgun stick retracted.
  3. Back off the stick, swing the blade partway up, check alignment and drive home.

After closing, the sleeve must cover the hole in the shaft.

If the hole remains visible, the blade must not be opened while the feeder is energised.

Opening

  1. Close the shotgun stick on the pull ring, pull clear of the top contact and swing down to the horizontal reset position.
  2. Reset the stick to the retracted position, lock the blade horizontally and lift it from the bottom contact.

Source: E2796 sheets 1–2

Telescopic switching-stick suitability · E2797

For SAPN-approved telescopic switching sticks on live equipment up to and including 33 kV. Every operation remains subject to an onsite risk assessment and E2804–E2809 limitations.

Protection Groups 1–4

1 Normal · 2 Tie · 3 Switching · 4 Special

Group 1

Normal operation

Normal OC, EOC and SEF settings.

Auto-reclose is generally non-auto where cable is included and may need to be manually enabled or disabled depending on the relay.

Group 2

Feeder tie or additional load

Raises the overcurrent setting to allow extra load.

SEF may also be raised when tying feeders with single-phase-to-earth transformers. On a relay with only two available groups, Group 2 may be used for high-speed operation.

Group 3

High-speed overhead switching

SEF blocked, EF raised for single-phase switching and reclosers set non-auto.

Used for authorised overhead, ground-level and glove-and-barrier switching as directed by the applicable procedure and protection information.

Group 4

Special temporary application

Settings vary to suit the specific application and are described on the protection summary card.

Where not specifically nominated, use requires advice or approval from Secondary Systems Planning.

High-speed settings

The source also lists “High Speed Settings” with no group specified. Treat this as a separate instruction—not a fifth group.

The exact group used can depend on the relay and the protection summary card.
